q: Old Monk, the cult Indian dark rum, was launched in which year?
r: Old Monk has been made since 1954, and built its following almost entirely by word of mouth.

q: Which spirit is the base of a classic Margarita?
r: Tequila, triple sec and lime. Mezcal makes it a Mezcal Margarita instead.

q: Feni, the fierce local spirit with a GI tag, comes from which Indian state?
r: Goa. Only feni made in Goa may legally use the name.

q: A Mojito is built on which spirit?
r: White rum, muddled with mint, lime and sugar, lengthened with soda.

q: What does IMFL stand for on Indian liquor labels?
o: Indian Ministry of Food and Liquor
r: Indian-Made Foreign Liquor: foreign-style spirits made in India. Foreign, made locally.

q: Which two ingredients join gin in a classic Negroni?
r: Equal parts gin, Campari and sweet vermouth.

q: Shikanji, the roadside cooler, is essentially which drink?
r: Lemon, sugar, black salt and roasted cumin in cold water. Chaas is buttermilk, aam panna is raw mango, jal-jeera is cumin water.

q: Which Indian rum is nicknamed for a religious figure?
r: Old Monk. Hercules, McDowell's and Contessa are all real Indian rums, but only one is a monk.

q: An Espresso Martini contains which of these?
r: Vodka, coffee liqueur, fresh espresso and sugar. Despite the name, no vermouth and no gin.

q: Aam panna, the summer cooler, is made from what?
r: Raw green mango, roasted and blended with cumin and black salt. Ripe mango makes a lassi or panha-style sweet drink, not panna.

q: Which country drinks the most whisky by volume?
r: India, by a wide margin. Roughly one in two bottles of whisky sold worldwide is poured there.

q: 'Neat' means a spirit served how?
o: Straight from the bottle, no ice, no chilling
r: Neat is room temperature and undiluted. 'Up' is chilled and strained; 'on the rocks' is over ice.

q: Which of these is NOT an Indian spirit or drink?
r: Pisco is Peruvian and Chilean. Feni, mahua and arrack are all South Asian.

q: A Piña Colada blends rum with which two?
r: Rum, pineapple juice and coconut cream. It's Puerto Rico's national drink.

q: In Indian bar slang, a 'chota peg' is what?
r: Chota is small, burra is large. The vocabulary marched in with the British army.

q: Which glass is traditionally used for an Old Fashioned?
r: A short, heavy-bottomed rocks glass, built over a large cube.

q: Toddy, the palm-sap drink, gets its English name from which Indian word?
r: From the Hindi tari, the sap of the palm tree. British sailors borrowed it for their hot whisky cure.

q: What is the primary flavour of gin?
r: Juniper, by law. Coriander and angelica are common supporting botanicals, but juniper must lead.

q: Somaek, the Korean bomb shot, mixes soju with what?
r: Soju plus maekju (beer). The name is a mash-up of both words.

q: Which Indian city is known as the country's craft-beer and pub capital?
r: Bengaluru earned it in the draught-beer boom of the 1980s and now has the most microbreweries.

q: A Daiquiri in its classic form is which three things?
r: Just rum, lime juice and sugar, shaken hard. Add mint and soda and you're heading toward a Mojito.

q: Kokum, used in Konkan coolers, is what kind of ingredient?
r: A sour, deep-magenta coastal fruit. It also makes solkadhi with coconut milk.

q: Which of these is a fortified wine?
r: Vermouth is wine fortified with spirit and infused with botanicals. The others are still or sparkling wines.

q: Nashik, in Maharashtra, is India's capital of what?
r: Wine. Vineyards along the Godavari supply most of India's wine.

q: What does 'on the rocks' mean?
r: Poured over ice. Simple as that.

q: Bhang, traditionally drunk at Holi, is stirred into which drink?
r: Thandai, the almond-rose milk. It's sold at government-licensed shops in cities like Varanasi.

q: A Bloody Mary's base spirit is which?
r: Vodka with tomato juice and spices. Made with gin it becomes a Red Snapper.

q: Which Indian state has been dry since 1960?
r: Gujarat, since 1960. Bihar, Mizoram and Nagaland introduced prohibition much later.

q: What is a 'mocktail'?
r: A cocktail without alcohol. Bartenders also call them zero-proof drinks.

q: Amrut, India's first single malt whisky, is distilled in which city?
r: Bengaluru. It launched in Glasgow in 2004 to prove Indian malt could compete.

q: Which of these is the odd one out as a cocktail base?
r: Angostura is bitters, dosed by the dash. The rest are base spirits.

q: Masala chaas is spiced what?
r: Thinned yogurt (buttermilk) with cumin, black salt and mint, drunk after lunch across India.

q: The Mai Tai belongs to which drinking style?
r: Tiki, the Polynesian-themed style invented in 1930s California. Trader Vic and Don the Beachcomber both claimed it.

q: Sula, Grover and Fratelli are Indian producers of what?
r: Wine. All three helped build India's modern wine industry.

q: What does 'ABV' measure?
r: Alcohol by volume, as a percentage. Proof, in the US system, is double the ABV.

q: A Cuba Libre is rum, cola and what?
r: A squeeze of lime is what separates a Cuba Libre from a plain rum and coke.

q: Tongba, drunk through a bamboo straw, is brewed from which grain?
r: Millet, in the Eastern Himalayas, topped up with hot water as the evening goes on.

q: Which cocktail is traditionally served in a copper mug?
r: The Moscow Mule. The Mint Julep uses a silver or pewter cup.

q: Solkadhi, the pink Konkan digestif, combines kokum with what?
r: Coconut milk, poured after fish curries the way other coasts pour digestifs.

q: Which is a rum-based classic?
r: Dark 'n' Stormy is dark rum with ginger beer. Sidecar is brandy, Vesper gin and vodka, Boulevardier whiskey.

q: Sake is produced by which process?
r: Sake is brewed from rice, so it's technically closer to beer. Soju and shochu are the distilled cousins.

q: Which Indian drink is described as 'cumin water'?
r: Jal-jeera: jal is water, jeera is cumin. Sharp, smoky and savoury.

q: The Aperol Spritz is topped with which wine?
r: Prosecco, with soda and Aperol, over lots of ice in a big glass.

q: Which is India's largest-selling category of spirits?
r: Whisky, overwhelmingly. Brandy leads in some southern states, but whisky dominates nationally.

q: Angostura bitters is best known for its oversized what?
r: Its label, famously too big for the bottle. Legend says one brother ordered bottles and the other labels.

q: A 'shot' in most bars is closest to which measure?
r: Roughly 30–60 ml depending on the country. A barspoon is about 5 ml.

q: Which Indian spirit is distilled from cashew or coconut?
r: Feni: cashew feni from the fruit, coconut feni from palm sap. Mahua comes from mahua flowers.

q: The Cosmopolitan is built on which spirit?
r: Citrus vodka, triple sec, cranberry and lime.

q: Mahua liquor is distilled from what part of the plant?
r: The sweet mahua blossoms. Banned as 'country liquor' under colonial rule, it's now being revived as a heritage spirit.

q: Which cocktail family does the Whiskey Sour belong to?
r: Sours: spirit, citrus and sweet. A flip adds a whole egg; a julep is spirit, sugar and mint over crushed ice.

q: What is India's Kasauli distillery famous for?
o: Being among Asia's oldest working distilleries
r: It has been running in the Himalayan foothills since the 1820s, still using Victorian copper stills.

q: The word 'punch' most likely comes from the Hindi 'panch', meaning what?
r: Five, for the drink's five parts: spirit, sugar, lemon, water and spice. It sailed to Europe with East India Company crews.

q: The Gin & Tonic began life as what?
r: Officers drank bitter quinine tonic against malaria; the gin ration made it bearable.

q: Which of these is NOT a genuine Old Fashioned variation?
o: Oaxaca Old Fashioned made with prosecco
Benton's Old Fashioned with bacon-fat-washed bourbon
Oaxaca Old Fashioned made with mezcal and tequila
r: The Oaxaca Old Fashioned uses reposado tequila and mezcal, never prosecco. The other three are all real, documented drinks.

q: A Patiala peg is named after a Maharaja of Patiala. What is it?
o: A peg measured against a polo mallet
A whisky served with soda in a silver cup
A double shot chased with lassi
r: An oversized measure, attributed to Maharaja Bhupinder Singh, whose hospitality left visiting cricket teams unfit for the morning.

q: India Pale Ale got its name from what?
o: The long sea voyage to India it had to survive
r: Brewers hopped and strengthened the ale so it would survive the months-long sail to India. It was never brewed there.

q: Why does the EU refuse to call most Indian 'whisky' whisky?
o: It is usually distilled from molasses, not grain
It is aged for under a year
r: Most IMFL whisky is molasses-based, so the EU classes it differently. A billion people call it whisky at the table anyway.

q: The Negroni was reportedly created when Count Camillo Negroni asked for what?
o: His Americano made with gin instead of soda
r: He asked for the Americano stiffened with gin in place of soda water, in Florence around 1919.

q: What makes a Negroni 'Sbagliato'?
o: It is served long over ice
r: Sbagliato means 'mistaken': a Milanese bartender reached for sparkling wine instead of gin and kept it.

q: Urrak, available only for a few months a year, is which stage of feni?
o: A blend of cashew and coconut feni
r: Urrak is the light first distillation, available roughly March to May, and almost never leaves Goa.

q: How did the cashew, source of Goan feni, reach India?
o: It is native to the Western Ghats
Dutch traders brought it from Indonesia
The Portuguese brought it from Brazil
The British brought it from Africa
r: The Portuguese carried it from Brazil to Goa in the 1500s, which makes feni a four-hundred-year-old fusion drink.

q: In a Martini, what does ordering it 'perfect' mean?
o: Equal parts dry and sweet vermouth
r: Perfect splits the vermouth half dry, half sweet. Dry means less vermouth; dirty adds olive brine.

q: Which is the correct build for a classic Sazerac?
o: Rye, sugar, Angostura bitters, vermouth rinse
Rye or cognac, sugar, Peychaud's bitters, absinthe rinse
r: New Orleans' Sazerac: spirit, sugar, Peychaud's, and an absinthe rinse. Peychaud's is the signature, not Angostura.

q: Judima, which won a GI tag in 2021, is made by which community?
r: The Dimasa people of Assam. It was the first traditional brew of the Northeast to get a GI tag.

q: Why are Mumbai's older bars called 'permit rooms'?
o: A 1949 law technically required drinkers to hold a permit
They were permitted to serve only IMFL
Only permit-holding clubs could serve foreigners
They needed a special licence to serve after midnight
r: The Bombay Prohibition Act of 1949 required a drinker's permit. The law faded; the name never left.

q: Which statement about dilution in cocktails is correct?
o: Dilution only matters for drinks served over ice
Dilution should be avoided entirely in quality cocktails
A properly shaken drink is 20–25% water from melted ice
Stirring adds more water than shaking
r: Melted ice is an ingredient. That water softens the alcohol and knits flavours; shaking dilutes more than stirring.

q: The Moscow Mule's copper mug originated as what?
o: A 1941 marketing pact between three struggling sellers
A Prohibition-era way to hide the drink
r: A vodka importer, a ginger beer maker and a copper mug seller pooled unsold stock in 1941.

q: Arrack, once southern India's everyday spirit, takes its name from an Arabic word meaning what?
r: From araq, meaning sweat, for the condensation dripping off the still.

q: Which is true of the Aviation cocktail?
o: Its blue-violet tint comes from crème de violette
Its colour comes from blue curaçao
r: Gin, maraschino, lemon and crème de violette, which gives the pale sky tint. It's shaken and strained.

q: Sharab, the Hindustani word for liquor, shares an Arabic root with which two English words?
r: All from shariba, to drink. One verb, three very different evenings.

q: What distinguishes a Collins from a Fizz?
o: A Fizz is stirred, not shaken
A Fizz uses gin; a Collins uses whiskey
A Collins is served tall over ice; a Fizz is shaken, often with egg white, and served shorter
r: Both are sours lengthened with soda, but the Collins is tall over ice while the Fizz is shaken hard, often with egg white, and served without much ice.

q: Kerala's toddy shops, the kallu shaapus, are also famous for what?
r: The kappa, karimeen and duck curries exist to keep pace with the toddy.

q: Which is the correct order of the Sour template?
o: 3 parts spirit, 1 part citrus, 2 parts sweet
1 part spirit, 2 parts citrus, 1 part sweet
1 part spirit, 1 part citrus, 2 parts sweet
2 parts spirit, 1 part citrus, 1 part sweet
r: 2:1:1 is the skeleton of the Daiquiri, Whiskey Sour, Margarita and Gimlet.

q: The Espresso Martini was created in 1980s London by which bartender?
r: Dick Bradsell, reportedly for a model who asked for something to wake her up, then mess her up.

q: Amrut's name comes from amrit, which in Hindu legend is what?
r: The nectar of immortality, churned from the ocean. A drinkable pun with scripture behind it.

q: Which claim about the Bloody Mary is accurate?
o: It was named for Queen Mary I by her own bartender
It was created in London during the Blitz
It was invented at New York's St. Regis and renamed in Paris
It was first mixed in 1920s Paris and renamed Red Snapper at New York's St. Regis
r: Harry's New York Bar in Paris in the 1920s; the St. Regis later adopted it and politely renamed it.

q: Sekmai yu, a distilled rice liquor, is named after what?
o: The festival it is drunk at
The clay pot it ferments in
r: Sekmai, a village in Manipur so associated with the drink that its name became the drink's.

q: What is the correct role of a 'rinse' in cocktail making?
o: Coating the glass with a strong ingredient, then pouring off the excess
Diluting a spirit with water before serving
r: A few millilitres of absinthe or smoky whisky coats the glass for aroma without weight.

q: Which is India's oldest surviving beer brand, brewed at Solan since the 1850s?
r: Lion, brewed in the Himalayan foothills at Solan, is considered Asia's oldest surviving beer brand.

q: In cocktail terms, what does 'expressing' a citrus twist mean?
o: Snapping the peel to mist its oils over the drink
Squeezing the juice into the drink
Rubbing the peel around the rim only
Twisting the peel into a spiral garnish
r: Snap the peel skin-side down over the surface to mist aromatic oils. It's seasoning, not decoration.

q: Kanji, the deep-purple Holi-week drink, is fermented from what?
r: Black carrots and mustard seeds left to ferment in the winter sun: North India's homemade kombucha.

q: What is the difference between shochu and soju?
o: Shochu is rice-only, soju is never rice
Shochu is Japanese, soju is Korean
Shochu is brewed, soju is distilled
r: Both are distilled East Asian spirits: shochu from Japan, soju from Korea.

q: The Indian Army's rum ration is traditionally which style?
r: Dark XXX rum has warmed high-altitude postings for decades, and Old Monk built its legend in those canteens.

q: Which is true of the Paper Plane, a modern classic from 2008?
o: It is stirred and served up with no garnish
It is equal parts bourbon, Aperol, amaro and lemon
It is equal parts gin, Aperol, amaro and lime
r: Equal parts bourbon, Aperol, Amaro Nonino and lemon juice. Named after the M.I.A. song.

q: Why was the sherry cobbler historically important?
o: It was the first drink served over crushed ice
It was the first cocktail sold in bottles
r: The most fashionable drink of the 1800s, and it single-handedly popularised the straw.

q: Neera and toddy are the same palm sap at different stages. What separates them?
o: Distillation: toddy is distilled, neera is not
The time of year they are tapped
Fermentation: neera is fresh and sweet, toddy has fermented
r: Morning sap drinks sweet as neera; by evening it has fermented into toddy on its own.

q: Which spirit is the base of a Pisco Sour?
o: Pisco, a South American grape brandy
r: Pisco is a grape brandy from Peru and Chile, shaken with lime, sugar and egg white.

q: Handia, brewed by Adivasi communities of eastern India, is what?
o: A rice beer fermented with herbal starter tablets
r: Rice beer fermented with herbal ranu tablets, offered to guests and gods alike.

q: What is a 'dry shake' for?
o: Whipping egg white or aquafaba into foam before shaking with ice
Shaking without spirits to test balance
r: Shake once without ice to build foam, then again with ice to chill. That's how sours get their dense white crown.

q: Which best describes the Highball ratio?
o: 1 part spirit to 5 parts mixer, no ice
2 parts spirit to 1 part mixer, stirred
1 part spirit to 1 part mixer, shaken
1 part spirit to 2–3 parts cold mixer, built over plenty of ice
r: Precision matters more than it looks: flat, warm or over-poured highballs fail.

q: In the Northeast, zutho and apong are both what?
o: Rice brews, Naga and Mising respectively
Millet spirits, Naga and Mising respectively
r: Rice becomes zutho for the Nagas and apong for the Mising of Assam, each with hereditary starter cakes.

q: Which is true of vermouth once opened?
o: It keeps indefinitely like a spirit
It should be refrigerated and used within about a month
It must be frozen to stop oxidation
r: It's wine. Refrigerate it and use it up; a dusty room-temperature bottle ruins Martinis.

q: Rajasthan's royal houses were known for distilling what?
o: Heritage liqueurs of saffron, dates and dry fruits
r: Recipes like kesar kasturi, with saffron, dates, dry fruits and dozens of spices, survived the palaces and are bottled again today.

q: Why is 'Old Fashioned' a retronym?
o: It was the oldest drink in the first cocktail book
It was renamed after Prohibition ended
1880s drinkers asked for their whiskey cocktail made 'the old-fashioned way'
It referred to old-fashioned glassware, not the drink
r: Tired of newfangled liqueurs and garnishes, drinkers asked for it made the old-fashioned way, and the name stuck.

q: Irish Coffee was invented where?
r: Invented at Foynes in the 1940s to thaw transatlantic passengers, then perfected at the Buena Vista in San Francisco.

q: Coorg is known for a distinctive household drinking tradition. What is it?
o: Homemade wines from coffee, ginger and gooseberry
r: Homemade wine is a household art there, and weddings are judged partly on the house pour.

q: What does 'GI tag' mean for a drink like feni or Judima?
o: Grain Identified: a labelling rule for the base ingredient
Geographical Indication: only producers from that place may use the name
r: Geographical Indication, the same protection Champagne enjoys.

q: The palm civet's nickname 'toddy cat' comes from what?
o: It raids the sap pots tied under palm blossoms
It was kept as a pet in toddy shops
Its call sounds like a tapper's whistle
r: It raids the collection pots toddy tappers tie under palm blossoms, and has a taste for the fermented ones.

q: Which is the correct distinction between bitters and amari?
o: Bitters are dosed by the dash; amari are sipped or poured in measures
Bitters are always Italian; amari are not
Amari are non-alcoholic; bitters are not
r: Bitters are intense tinctures used as seasoning; amari are bitter liqueurs consumed in real measures.

q: Goa's port-style fortified wines are a legacy of what?
o: Four and a half centuries of Portuguese rule
r: No Goan susegad lunch is complete without a small glass of it.

q: What is the difference between a strain and a double strain?
o: A double strain adds a fine mesh to catch pulp and ice shards
A double strain means straining twice into two glasses
A double strain uses two Hawthorne strainers
A double strain is straining before and after chilling
r: Add a fine mesh strainer over the glass when pulp, herb flecks or ice shards would spoil a stemmed drink.

q: Terracotta stills found in the Gandhara region suggest distillation in South Asia dates back how far?
r: Roughly two thousand years, among the earliest evidence of distillation anywhere.

q: The Singapore Sling was created at which hotel?
r: The Long Bar at Raffles, around 1915, where sweeping peanut shells onto the floor is still encouraged.

q: India's craft gin wave of the late 2010s rose mainly out of which state?
r: Goa, distilled with local botanicals like gondhoraj lime, Himalayan juniper and curry leaf.

q: What does 'susegad', often linked to Goan drinking culture, mean?
r: From the Portuguese sossegado: a relaxed, unhurried contentment. It's a way of drinking as much as a mood.

q: Gondhoraj lebu, prized in modern Indian cocktails, is associated with which region?
r: Kolkata's beloved gondhoraj lime turned the gimlet into a modern Indian bar classic.

q: Which cocktail is officially recognised as Puerto Rico's national drink?
r: The Piña Colada. Two San Juan bars have argued for decades over which blended the first.

q: Frederic Tudor, the 'Ice King', made cold drinks fashionable by doing what?
o: Shipping New England lake ice to the tropics in the 1830s
r: He shipped Boston lake ice to the tropics, and iced drinks became a flex of empire.

q: American Prohibition had which lasting effect on cocktails worldwide?
o: It made gin illegal in Britain too
It ended the cocktail as a category
It created the first cocktail books
It exported bartenders and the golden age of mixing to Europe and Havana
r: Out-of-work bartenders sailed for London, Paris and Havana, taking the craft with them.

q: Vermouth takes its name from Wermut, the German word for what?
r: Wormwood, the bittering herb in its earliest recipes.

q: Jägermeister's name translates as what?
r: Hunt master. The glowing stag honours the patron saints of hunters; the 56-botanical recipe dates to 1934.

q: Ernest Hemingway's Daiquiri at El Floridita, the 'Papa Doble', was distinctive how?
r: Double rum, no sugar. The bar still serves it in his honour.

q: Which is the correct definition of 'proof' in the US system?
o: The same as the ABV percentage
r: 80 proof equals 40% ABV.

q: What is the traditional purpose of a 'toast'?
o: Spiced toasted bread was floated in communal wine to season it
Toasting glasses to check for cracks
Warming the wine with hot bread
r: The guest honoured by the custom 'got the toast'. The word outlived the bread.

q: 'Happy hour' began as slang in which context?
o: The US Navy's scheduled entertainment period
r: US Navy slang from the 1910s for a ship's entertainment period. The drinking sense came ashore during Prohibition.

q: How did the Martini change over the last century?
o: It got drier: Victorian versions used equal parts gin and sweet vermouth
It gained bitters that were never there originally
It switched from vodka to gin
r: Victorian recipes used equal parts gin and sweet vermouth, plus bitters. It dried out over a century.

q: Cachaça differs from rum how?
o: It must be aged in oak for three years
It is distilled from fresh sugarcane juice, not molasses
r: Fresh-pressed cane juice, and Brazil was distilling it decades before the Caribbean got its first stills.

q: The Margarita's name means 'daisy' in Spanish. Why does that matter?
o: The tequila Daisy appears in print decades before the Margarita origin legends
It was named after a flower farm
The glass was called a daisy glass
Daisies were used as the original garnish
r: The Daisy was an established drink family, and the tequila Daisy predates the half-dozen Margarita origin stories bartenders still argue about.

q: Which is true about ice clarity?
o: Cloudiness comes from mineral content only
Clear ice is colder than cloudy ice
Cloudiness is trapped air and impurities; directional freezing gives clear ice
r: Directional freezing pushes air and impurities out, giving clear, slow ice.

q: Tiki as a bar style was invented where?
r: Don the Beachcomber opened in 1934 in California; Trader Vic followed, and the two feuded for decades.

q: Which best describes 'sura' in Indian history?
o: A distilled spirit of the Mughal court
A fermented drink named in the Rigveda over three thousand years ago
r: Sura appears in the Rigveda, making India home to some of the oldest recorded drinking culture anywhere.

q: The B-52 shot is layered in which order, bottom to top?
o: Coffee liqueur, Irish cream, triple sec
Triple sec, coffee liqueur, Irish cream
Irish cream, coffee liqueur, triple sec
Coffee liqueur, triple sec, Irish cream
r: Density does the work: coffee liqueur sinks, then Irish cream, then triple sec floats.

q: Which is the defining technique difference between a Martini and a Daiquiri?
o: The Martini is stirred; the Daiquiri is shaken because it contains citrus
The Martini is shaken; the Daiquiri is stirred
Both are stirred, only the glass differs
Both are shaken, only the spirit differs
r: Shake anything with citrus, dairy or egg. Stir spirit-only drinks so they stay silky and clear.

q: What is aquafaba used for in cocktails?
o: A clarifying agent for milk punches
A vegan substitute for egg white foam
r: Chickpea-tin liquid whips like egg white, giving sours their foam without the egg.

q: Which pair is correctly matched?
r: Peychaud's is the Sazerac's signature bitters, born in New Orleans like the drink.

q: Why is a coupe often preferred over a V-shaped Martini glass in modern bars?
o: It spills less and drinks better
r: The shallow stemmed saucer replaced the V behind most serious bars for exactly that reason.

q: A 'flip' differs from a sour how?
o: A flip contains a whole egg
r: A flip uses a whole egg; a sour with egg white only is a silver sour.

q: What is orgeat?
r: An almond syrup, essential in the Mai Tai and much of tiki.

q: Which is true of falernum?
o: A Barbadian spiced syrup or liqueur with lime, almond and clove
r: A Barbadian sweetener, spiced with lime, almond, ginger and clove, common in tiki drinks.

q: The Last Word cocktail is equal parts of which four?
r: Equal parts gin, green Chartreuse, maraschino liqueur and lime juice, revived from Prohibition-era Detroit.

q: What does 'building' a drink mean?
o: Assembling it in a mixing glass first
Making it directly in the serving glass
r: Ice first, then each ingredient in order, then a brief stir. The method behind every highball.

q: Which cocktail traditionally uses a silver or pewter cup?
r: The Mint Julep. The Moscow Mule uses copper.

q: What is verjus?
o: The pressed juice of unripe grapes
r: Unripe grape juice, tart without alcohol, useful in zero-alcohol drinks.

q: The Corpse Reviver No. 2 contains a rinse or dash of what?
r: Gin, Cointreau, Lillet Blanc, lemon and a whisper of absinthe. Harry Craddock warned against four in quick succession.

q: What is 'fat washing'?
o: Adding cream to soften a spirit
Infusing a spirit with fat, then freezing and removing it to keep flavour without texture
Washing glassware in fat to coat it
Skimming fat off a milk punch
r: Benton's Old Fashioned uses bacon-fat-washed bourbon, made this way.

q: Which is correct about Chartreuse?
o: It is a Trappist beer liqueur
It is flavoured primarily with mint
It is a Spanish herbal brandy
It is made by Carthusian monks from around 130 botanicals
r: Carthusian monks have made it in France for centuries; green is stronger, yellow softer and sweeter.

q: What is a 'milk punch' clarified with?
o: Milk, which curdles and is strained out, leaving a clear drink
r: Acid curdles the milk; straining leaves a silky, clear punch that keeps for months.

q: Which is true of the Jungle Bird?
o: It is a gin and pineapple tiki drink
It combines dark rum with Campari and pineapple
r: A Malaysian tiki classic from the 1970s: dark rum, Campari, pineapple and lime.

q: What separates an aperitif from a digestif?
o: Aperitifs are drunk before a meal to open the appetite; digestifs after, to settle
r: Before versus after the meal. Campari and vermouth aperitifs; amari and brandy digestifs.

q: Lillet Blanc is best described as what?
r: A Bordeaux wine-based aperitif, used in the Vesper and Corpse Reviver No. 2.

q: Which best describes mezcal versus tequila?
o: Tequila is always smoky, mezcal never is
All tequila is mezcal by definition, but only blue agave from set regions makes tequila
Mezcal must be made from blue agave
r: Mezcal is the broad category from any agave; tequila is the blue-agave subset from designated regions.

q: Genever is best described as what?
o: The malty Dutch ancestor of gin
r: Malt-wine based and juniper-flavoured, it's the Dutch forerunner of London Dry gin.

q: Which is the correct description of an Amaretto Sour done well?
o: Amaretto, bourbon for backbone, lemon and egg white
r: The modern spec adds a little bourbon so the almond sweetness has a spine.

q: What does 'IBA' mean on a cocktail listing?
o: International Bartenders Association, which maintains official recipes
r: The IBA maintains a list of official cocktails, split into Unforgettables, Contemporary Classics and New Era drinks.

q: Which is true of the Vesper as written by Ian Fleming?
o: It uses rum and Lillet, shaken
It uses gin and dry vermouth, stirred
It uses gin, vodka and Kina Lillet, shaken
r: Three of gin, one of vodka, half of Kina Lillet, shaken and served with a lemon peel.

q: What is the role of saline or a pinch of salt in a cocktail?
o: It suppresses bitterness and lifts perceived sweetness and aroma
r: A tiny amount rounds off bitterness and makes flavours read brighter, the same as in cooking.

q: Which of these gins is closest in style to a London Dry?
o: A juniper-forward dry gin from anywhere in the world
r: London Dry is a production style, not a place. Old Tom is sweeter, sloe gin is a liqueur, genever is malty.

q: Why did quinine become associated with tonic water?
o: It was an antimalarial, and soda and sugar made it drinkable
It gave the water its fizz
r: The bitter antimalarial needed soda and sugar to be palatable, and gin finished the job.

q: What is a 'pousse-café'?
o: A layered shot built by density
r: Multiple liqueurs floated in distinct layers, poured slowly over a barspoon.

q: Which is correct about the Sidecar's proportions in the classic French school?
o: Two cognac, one Cointreau, one lemon
Three cognac, one Cointreau, one lemon
Equal parts cognac and lemon, no Cointreau
Equal parts cognac, Cointreau and lemon
r: The French school pours equal parts; the English school prefers 2:1:1. Both are considered correct.

q: What does it mean to 'batch' cocktails?
o: Pre-mixing multiple servings in advance, often with water for dilution
r: Pre-mix the recipe scaled up, add the dilution water, chill, and pour on demand.

q: Which claim about absinthe is true?
o: It is distilled from wormwood alone
Thujone's hallucinogenic reputation was overstated and it is legal in most countries today
r: The wormwood scare was overblown; absinthe is legal in most countries and is anise-forward.

q: What is the difference between a Gimlet and a Daiquiri?
o: Gimlet uses lemon, Daiquiri uses lime
Gimlet is gin and lime; Daiquiri is rum and lime
r: Same sour skeleton, different spirit: gin versus rum.

q: Which is true of the Ranch Water tradition of West Texas?
o: It must be served in a copper mug
It uses sparkling wine, not water
Some drink part of the mineral water straight from the bottle and mix the rest in it
r: Tequila, lime and very cold sparkling mineral water, often built right in the bottle.

q: What is 'Old Tom' gin?
o: A slightly sweetened historical gin style
r: A lightly sweetened style bridging genever and London Dry, and the correct gin for a Martinez or Tom Collins.

q: Which best explains why highball glasses are tall and narrow?
o: Less surface area means bubbles escape more slowly
They keep the drink colder by shape alone
r: Narrow means less surface for carbonation to escape from, so the drink stays lively.

q: Which Indian whisky brands are among the world's best-selling by volume?
o: Solan No.1, Bagpiper and Director's Special
McDowell's No.1, Officer's Choice and Imperial Blue
r: These mass-market IMFL brands each outsell the biggest Scotch labels many times over. The second list is India's premium malts, not the volume leaders.

q: Paul John single malt is distilled in which state?
r: Goa. Amrut is Bengaluru, Rampur is Uttar Pradesh, and Kasauli is Himachal.

q: Rampur single malt comes from a distillery in which state?
r: Rampur, Uttar Pradesh, at the Radico Khaitan distillery.

q: Why does Indian whisky mature faster than Scotch?
o: Indian malt is distilled to a lower strength
Indian barrels are smaller by law
India's heat causes far greater annual evaporation and faster interaction with the oak
r: The tropical climate drives an 'angel's share' several times Scotland's, so three Indian years can taste like a decade of Scotch.

q: What is the 'angel's share'?
o: Spirit lost to evaporation during barrel ageing
The portion left in the cask after bottling
The first spirit off the still
r: Evaporation through the cask. In India's heat it can exceed 10% a year.

q: Which is a traditional drink of Sikkim and Darjeeling?
r: Chhaang, a Himalayan fermented barley or millet brew. Handia is eastern India, Judima Assam, mahua central India.

q: Thandai, the Holi drink, is built on which base?
o: Milk with almonds, fennel and rose
r: A milk base with almonds, fennel, pepper, rose and saffron. Bhang is sometimes added.

q: Which Indian state is the largest consumer of brandy?
o: Kerala and Tamil Nadu lead brandy consumption
r: Southern states, especially Kerala and Tamil Nadu, are brandy strongholds while whisky leads nationally.

q: What is 'country liquor' in Indian regulatory language?
o: Any spirit made in rural areas
Traditional local spirits taxed and licensed separately from IMFL
r: Indigenous spirits like mahua and arrack sit in a separate, cheaper regulatory class from IMFL.

q: Which of these is a genuine risk associated with illicit liquor in India?
r: Methanol contamination in hooch has caused mass-casualty tragedies, which is why licensed production matters.

q: Kingfisher, India's best-known beer brand, belongs to which group?
r: United Breweries. Mohan Meakin makes Old Monk and Solan No.1; Radico makes Rampur.

q: Old Monk is produced by which company?
r: Mohan Meakin, whose Kasauli and Ghaziabad operations date back to the 19th century.

q: What is 'desi daru'?
r: Literally 'local liquor', the everyday term for country-made spirits.

q: Which Indian festival is most associated with bhang-laced thandai?
r: Holi. It's a centuries-old tradition, licensed in cities like Varanasi.

q: Which Indian city has the most microbreweries?
r: Bengaluru leads, thanks partly to Karnataka's early microbrewery-friendly rules.

q: What is the legal drinking age in most of India?
o: It varies by state, from 18 to 25
r: Alcohol is a state subject, so the age ranges from 18 in Goa to 25 in Maharashtra and Delhi.

q: Why does liquor pricing vary so much between Indian states?
o: Alcohol is a state subject, so each state sets its own excise duty
r: Excise is a major state revenue source, so duties and retail models differ sharply across borders.

q: Which drink is traditionally offered to guests in parts of Nagaland?
r: Zutho is Naga; Judima is Dimasa (Assam), handia is eastern-Indian Adivasi, chhaang Himalayan.

q: Apong is associated with which community?
r: The Mising people of Assam brew apong from rice with hereditary starter cakes.

q: Kesar kasturi is what kind of drink?
o: A Rajasthani heritage liqueur of saffron and spices
r: A royal Rajasthani liqueur with saffron, dates, dry fruits and dozens of spices.

q: Which is true of Indian craft gin brands like Greater Than and Stranger & Sons?
o: They use Indian botanicals such as gondhoraj lime and coriander
They are all made in Kerala
They are distilled in Scotland and bottled in India
r: The Indian gin wave is defined by local botanicals: gondhoraj lime, curry leaf, Himalayan juniper and more.

q: What is 'tharra'?
o: A country liquor distilled from sugarcane or jaggery
r: A north Indian country liquor from fermented sugarcane or jaggery.

q: Which best describes Goa's 'sunburn' of drinking rules compared to other states?
o: Goa prohibits spirits but allows beer
Goa has the highest excise in India
Goa restricts sales to hotels only
Goa has relatively liberal licensing and lower excise, so drinks cost less
r: Lower excise and liberal licensing are exactly why Goa became a drinking destination.

q: Which Indian drink is famously served in an earthen or bamboo vessel?
r: Tongba is served in a bamboo mug with a bamboo straw, topped up with hot water.

q: What does 'sundowner' mean in Indian and colonial drinking usage?
o: A drink served with a sunset view charge
The last drink of the night
r: A sunset drink, a habit inherited from colonial club culture.

q: Which is the correct pairing of Indian drink to region?
r: Kokum and coconut milk make solkadhi, poured along the Konkan coast after fish curries.

q: Sula Vineyards is located near which city?
r: Nashik, the heart of India's wine country.

q: Which Indian mixer is a common base for local highballs?
r: Soda and cola dominate; Thums Up in particular has a devoted following with rum and whisky.

q: What is unusual about alcohol advertising in India?
o: It is permitted only in English
It requires a health warning voiceover
It is allowed only on television
Direct advertising is banned, so brands use 'surrogate' products like soda and music CDs
r: Direct liquor advertising is prohibited, which is why you see brand-named soda, water and music events.

q: Which is true of 'dry days' in India?
o: They are days when only beer may be sold
Alcohol sales are banned on certain national holidays and election days
They apply only to bars, not shops
r: Republic Day, Independence Day, Gandhi Jayanti and polling days are commonly dry.

q: Which best describes a 'thekha' or 'theka'?
o: A bar attached to a hotel
r: The licensed retail liquor shop, a fixture of Indian towns.

q: Toddy tapping requires the tapper to do what daily?
o: Boil the sap to stop fermentation
Climb palms twice a day to collect sap
r: In Kerala tappers walk rope bridges between palm crowns twice a day. Fermentation happens on its own.

q: Which is India's oldest continuously operating brewery region?
r: Solan, where Lion beer has been brewed since the 1850s.

q: Which spirit category has grown fastest among young urban Indians in recent years?
r: Craft gin, driven by the Goa-led wave of local-botanical distilleries.

q: What is a 'quarter' in Indian liquor retail?
r: A 180 ml bottle, the ubiquitous 'quarter'. 90 ml is a 'nip' and 375 ml a 'half'.

q: In Indian bar usage, what is a 'nip'?
r: A 90 ml bottle, the smallest common retail size.

q: Which is correct about jamun, used in modern Indian cocktails?
o: A dark purple monsoon berry with an astringent finish
r: The Indian blackberry, tart and astringent, excellent in sours and vodka drinks.

q: Which pair of Indian ingredients would you find in a jal-jeera?
r: Roasted cumin, black salt, tamarind and mint make it sharp and savoury.

q: What is khus syrup made from?
r: Vetiver root, prized as a cooling summer flavour in North India.

q: Kala khatta, the gola syrup, is characterised by which flavour profile?
o: Sweet, sour and salty with black salt
r: Sweet-sour-salty with black salt, the Mumbai gola-cart classic.

q: Which is true about 'permit' requirements for visitors to Gujarat?
o: Visitors may not drink at all
Only foreign passport holders may drink
Permits are issued only to residents
Visitors can obtain a liquor permit to drink legally
r: Gujarat has been dry since 1960, but visitors can get a government-issued permit.

q: Which Indian drink tradition involves a starter cake or tablet passed down through families?
o: Northeast rice brews like apong and zutho
r: Hereditary starter cultures, like ranu tablets for handia, are treated as heirlooms.

q: Which is a genuine Indian gin botanical used by local distillers?
r: Curry leaf, gondhoraj lime, Himalayan juniper and coriander are all used in Indian craft gins.

q: What is 'sharbat' in the Indian drinks vocabulary?
o: A sweet fruit or flower syrup diluted with water
r: A syrup base, diluted to drink. Rooh Afza is the most famous commercial example.

q: Rooh Afza is best described as what?
r: A rose-forward sharbat concentrate, iconic across South Asia, especially in Ramadan.

q: Which is true of the Indian bar scene's 'Kokum Sour' style drinks?
o: They apply the classic sour template to Indian souring agents
They are traditional recipes from the 1800s
r: Modern Indian bartending swaps citrus for kokum, tamarind or gondhoraj in the 2:1:1 sour skeleton.

q: Which best describes India's position in global whisky production?
o: It produces and consumes more whisky by volume than any other country
It is a small niche producer
It exports more than it consumes
r: India dominates by volume, though most of it is molasses-based IMFL rather than grain whisky.

q: Which Indian single malt won early international acclaim by launching in Glasgow?
r: Amrut launched in Glasgow in 2004, deliberately taking on Scotch on home ground.

q: Indri, a recent award-winning Indian single malt, is distilled in which state?
r: Indri, Haryana, from Piccadily Distilleries.

q: What does the term 'susu' or 'sulai' refer to in parts of India?
r: Regional slang for locally brewed, often illicit, liquor.

q: Which is a traditional Ladakhi or Tibetan-influenced brew?
r: Chhaang, a barley or millet brew of the Himalayas.

q: Sea buckthorn, used in Ladakhi drinks, is prized for what?
o: Its intense tartness and vitamin content
r: The tart orange 'leh berry' makes sharp, bright juices and cordials.

q: Which James Bond film popularised the phrase 'shaken, not stirred'?
o: It runs through the series, first spoken on screen in Goldfinger
r: Bond orders it in the novels, and the exact screen phrasing lands in Goldfinger. Purists note shaking a Martini is technically wrong.

q: In Mad Men, which drink is Don Draper most associated with?
r: The Old Fashioned, which the show helped revive for a new generation.

q: The Cosmopolitan's 1990s boom is widely credited to which TV show?
r: Sex and the City made it the decade's defining cocktail.

q: 'The Dude' in The Big Lebowski drinks which cocktail?
r: The White Russian, which he calls a Caucasian.

q: Which cocktail features in the title of a famous Jimmy Buffett song?
r: Margaritaville. Rupert Holmes handled the Piña Colada.

q: 'Escape (The Piña Colada Song)' was recorded by whom?
r: Rupert Holmes, 1979. The song is actually about a couple answering each other's personal ads.

q: Which Bollywood song title references a drink measure?
o: Songs referencing 'peg' are common in Punjabi pop
r: Punjabi and Bollywood pop reference 'peg' frequently, reflecting how deeply the word sits in Indian drinking slang.

q: Which drink is associated with New Orleans' Mardi Gras and its Hurricane glass?
r: The Hurricane, though the Sazerac, Ramos Gin Fizz and Vieux Carré are all New Orleans classics too.

q: The Vieux Carré cocktail is named after what?
o: The French Quarter of New Orleans
r: Vieux Carré is the French Quarter, where it was created at the Hotel Monteleone.

q: Which cocktail is traditionally served at the Kentucky Derby?
r: The Mint Julep, by the tens of thousands.

q: Which drink is the traditional choice at Wimbledon alongside strawberries?
r: Pimm's No. 1 with lemonade, fruit and mint.

q: Which cocktail shares its name with a Manhattan borough?
r: All three are real cocktails: the Bronx, the Brooklyn and the Queens Park Swizzle. A question where the options aren't mutually exclusive.

q: The Bee's Knees cocktail dates from which era, and why the name?
o: Victorian London, named for a beekeeper
Prohibition, when honey masked rough bathtub gin
r: Gin, honey and lemon. The honey helped hide the taste of poor-quality Prohibition gin.

q: Which spirit does a Sidecar use?
r: Cognac with Cointreau and lemon.

q: What is the 'Death in the Afternoon' cocktail, and who created it?
o: Gin and champagne, by Harry Craddock
Rum and absinthe, by Trader Vic
Whiskey and absinthe, by Jerry Thomas
Absinthe and champagne, attributed to Hemingway
r: Absinthe topped with champagne, attributed to Hemingway and named after his bullfighting book.

q: Jerry Thomas is significant to cocktail history because he did what?
o: Published the first bartender's guide in 1862
r: 'How to Mix Drinks; or, The Bon Vivant's Companion' (1862) is the first known cocktail book.

q: The Savoy Cocktail Book was written by whom?
r: Harry Craddock of the American Bar at the Savoy, 1930. Ada Coleman preceded him there and created the Hanky Panky.

q: Ada Coleman, one of history's most famous bartenders, created which drink?
r: The Hanky Panky, at the Savoy's American Bar. Dick Bradsell created the Bramble decades later.

q: The Bramble was created in 1980s London by which bartender?
r: Dick Bradsell, who also gave us the Espresso Martini.

q: Which is true of the Ramos Gin Fizz?
o: It is shaken for a famously long time to build its foam
r: Gin, cream, egg white, citrus and orange flower water, shaken at length for that cloud-like head.

q: Which trend defined cocktail bars in the 2010s?
o: The craft cocktail revival with house syrups, clarification and low-waste bars
r: House-made everything, historical revivals, and later a sustainability push against waste.

q: What is the 'low- and no-alcohol' trend driven by?
o: Higher taxes on strong spirits only
Health-conscious drinkers wanting the ritual without the alcohol
r: Sober-curious drinking pushed distilled non-alcoholic spirits and serious zero-alcohol menus into the mainstream.

q: What does 'sober curious' mean?
o: Abstaining one month a year only
Choosing to drink less or not at all without identifying as fully sober
r: A cultural shift toward moderation, which reshaped bar menus worldwide.

q: What is a 'low-waste' or 'closed-loop' bar?
o: A bar that uses citrus husks, peels and offcuts instead of binning them
A bar that never batches drinks
A bar that serves only local spirits
A bar with no single-use glassware
r: Husk cordials, oleo-saccharum from peels, and reusing every part of an ingredient.

q: What is oleo-saccharum?
o: Sugar-extracted citrus peel oil, used in punches
r: Sugar draws the oil out of citrus peels, creating an intensely aromatic syrup used in classic punches.

q: Which is true of the modern 'highball renaissance', especially in Japan?
o: It means highballs made with sparkling wine
It is a return to pre-mixed cans only
Whisky highballs are treated with precision on ice, dilution and carbonation
It refers to taller glassware only
r: Japanese bars turned the highball into a discipline: hard ice, cold soda, exact ratios, minimal stirring.

q: What is 'clarified milk punch' prized for?
o: A silky texture and long shelf life with a clear appearance
r: The milk curdles, is strained out, and leaves a clear, velvety drink that keeps for months.

q: Which is a genuine trend in Indian bars in recent years?
o: A ban on all imported spirits
Regional Indian ingredients in classic templates
A shift away from whisky entirely
r: Kokum, gondhoraj, jamun, curry leaf and toddy appearing in sours, spritzes and highballs.

q: What does 'terroir' mean when applied to spirits?
o: The influence of place, climate and raw material on flavour
r: Borrowed from wine: place shapes flavour, whether in agave, cane or grain.

q: Which is a rising category globally, especially among younger drinkers?
r: RTDs have grown fast for convenience and consistent quality.

q: What is 'agave spirit' terminology likely to include beyond tequila and mezcal?
r: Raicilla and bacanora are agave spirits with their own regions; sotol comes from a related plant.

q: What is the significance of the 'Death & Co' and 'PDT' bars?
o: They created the first RTD cocktails
They shaped the modern New York craft cocktail movement
r: Both are landmarks of the 2000s New York cocktail renaissance, and their books shaped bars worldwide.

q: Which best describes the 'World's 50 Best Bars' list?
o: A ranking of bar sales volume
A list of the oldest bars in the world
An annual global ranking that has included Indian bars in recent years
r: Indian bars have begun appearing on it, a marker of how fast the scene has matured.

q: What does 'batching for service' solve in a busy bar?
o: Speed and consistency across many drinks
r: Pre-measured mixes mean every drink tastes the same and lands fast.

q: Which is true of barrel-aged cocktails?
o: The whole cocktail rests in wood, softening and integrating it
Only the base spirit is aged
They must be aged for a year minimum
r: Ageing a Negroni or Manhattan in wood rounds it out; vermouth-containing drinks are common candidates.

q: What is the purpose of a 'garnish' in serious bartending?
r: A mint sprig or citrus twist sits at the nose and changes every sip. If it does neither, leave it off.

q: Which claim about the Manhattan is correct?
o: Rye or bourbon, sweet vermouth and bitters, stirred
Whiskey, sweet vermouth and citrus, shaken
Rye, dry vermouth and bitters, shaken
r: 2:1 whiskey to sweet vermouth with bitters, stirred and served up or on a cube.

q: The Boulevardier differs from a Negroni how?
r: Bourbon or rye in place of gin, often with a slightly higher whiskey proportion.

q: Which is true of the Americano cocktail?
r: The Negroni's ancestor: Campari, sweet vermouth and soda water.

q: What is 'Suze'?
r: A bitter French gentian-root aperitif, distinctively earthy.

q: Fernet-Branca is best described as what?
o: An intensely bitter Italian amaro, popular as a bartender's shot
r: Fiercely bitter and menthol-driven, famously the 'bartender's handshake'.

q: Which is true of the Paloma?
o: Tequila with grapefruit soda and lime
r: Mexico's everyday tequila drink, far more common there than the Margarita.

q: What is 'chilli-salt rim' or Tajín used for?
o: A garnish for tiki drinks only
A savoury-spicy rim on Mexican-style drinks
r: Chilli, lime and salt seasoning, used on Micheladas, Palomas and fruit.

q: A Michelada is built on what?
o: Beer with lime, salt and savoury seasonings
r: Mexican beer cocktail: lime, salt, hot sauce and sometimes clamato.

q: What distinguishes a Caipirinha from a Daiquiri?
o: Cachaça and muddled lime wheels rather than rum and lime juice
r: Cachaça, muddled lime and sugar, built in the glass over crushed ice.

q: Singani, a lesser-known grape spirit, comes from which country?
r: Bolivia, distilled from high-altitude Muscat grapes.

q: Which is true of aquavit?
o: A Scandinavian spirit flavoured with caraway or dill
r: Caraway or dill-forward, traditionally drunk with food in Scandinavia.

q: What is 'raki' and where is it from?
r: Turkey's anise spirit, which turns cloudy with water, like ouzo and pastis.

q: Why do anise spirits like raki, ouzo and pastis turn cloudy with water?
o: The louche effect: anise oils are insoluble in water and form an emulsion
r: Called the louche. Essential oils drop out of solution, clouding the glass.

q: Which best describes 'navy strength' spirits?
o: Bottled at 57% ABV or above, historically so spilled spirit wouldn't ruin gunpowder
r: 57% was the 'proof' point at which gunpowder soaked in spirit would still ignite.

q: Which is true of sherry styles?
o: Fino is dry and pale; Pedro Ximénez is intensely sweet
r: Fino and manzanilla are dry and delicate; oloroso is richer; PX is dessert-sweet.

q: Which is true of the Tommy's Margarita?
o: It replaces triple sec with agave syrup
r: Created at Tommy's in San Francisco: tequila, lime and agave nectar, no orange liqueur.

q: What is the difference between crème de cacao and chocolate liqueur in practice?
o: Crème de cacao is typically drier and used in classics like the Alexander
r: Crème de cacao (white or dark) is the classic cocktail ingredient; modern chocolate liqueurs are often sweeter and richer.

q: Which is true of Irish cream liqueurs in cocktails?
o: Acid can curdle them, which is why layered shots are drunk quickly
r: That's exactly why an Irish Slammer is drunk straight down before it curdles in the stout.

q: Which is true of Indian rum's flavour reputation?
o: Indian rums are legally required to be spiced
Indian rum is distilled from grapes
Indian rums are all unaged and dry
Old Monk is known for a pronounced vanilla character
r: Old Monk's distinct vanilla note is its signature, aged in oak and bottled at 42.8% ABV.

q: What is unusual about how Old Monk built its brand?
o: Essentially no advertising, only word of mouth
r: One of the world's best-selling rums with almost no advertising for decades.

q: Which Indian drink would you most likely be served after a heavy fish curry on the Konkan coast?
r: Solkadhi, kokum in coconut milk, acts as a digestive.

q: Which souring agent is most associated with Bengali cocktails?
r: Gondhoraj lebu, intensely fragrant, is Kolkata's pride.

q: What is the practical difference between a 'peg' and a 'shot' in Indian usage?
o: A peg is a measured pour of spirit, typically 30 or 60 ml, usually drunk with a mixer
A shot is larger than a peg
A peg is always drunk neat in one go
r: Pegs are how Indians measure whisky pours: chota 30 ml, burra 60 ml, usually taken long with soda or water.

q: Which is a real risk of 'hooch' tragedies in India?
o: Methanol added or produced during unregulated distillation
r: Methanol poisoning from illicit distillation has caused repeated mass-casualty incidents.

q: Which cocktail would best showcase mahua's floral character?
o: A sour, where its floral notes sit against citrus
r: Mahua's honeyed, floral profile shines with acid, the way a good sour frames any base spirit.

q: Which claim about black salt (kala namak) in drinks is accurate?
o: It is used only in alcoholic drinks
It adds a sulphurous, savoury tang used across Indian coolers
r: Its distinct sulphurous savour defines shikanji, jal-jeera, aam panna and kala khatta.

q: What is the traditional vessel for serving chaas or lassi in much of India?
o: A tall steel or brass tumbler
r: Steel and brass tumblers are the everyday standard.

q: Which best explains why Indian bartenders reach for jaggery?
o: It is less sweet than sugar
It adds a mineral, molasses-like depth a plain syrup cannot
r: Unrefined cane gur brings caramel and mineral notes, excellent with dark rum and whisky.

q: Which is India's most widely consumed alcoholic drink category by volume, including country liquor?
r: India is a spirits market above all, with whisky far ahead of beer by volume of alcohol consumed.

q: Which Indian state pioneered microbrewery-friendly regulation, fuelling the craft beer boom?
r: Karnataka's rules let Bengaluru's microbrewery scene flourish first.

q: What is the significance of the 1949 Bombay Prohibition Act today?
o: It applies only to Mumbai city
It still technically underpins Maharashtra's permit system and the name 'permit room'
r: The Act survives in amended form, which is why permits and 'permit rooms' persist.

q: Which of these Indian drinks is fermented rather than merely mixed?
r: Kanji ferments black carrots and mustard seeds in the sun. The others are fresh mixes.

q: Which is true of the 'leh berry' or sea buckthorn drinks of Ladakh?
o: They are tart, vitamin-rich cordials made from a hardy high-altitude berry
They are distilled into a local spirit
They are fermented into wine only
They are sweet and low in acid
r: Sharp and bright, they thrive in Ladakh's extreme climate.

q: Which Indian ingredient would you use to make a drink 'astringent and purple'?
r: Jamun, the Indian blackberry. Kokum is magenta and sour; khus is green and cooling.

q: What best describes the role of curry leaf in modern Indian gin?
o: An aromatic botanical giving a distinctly South Indian nose
r: Distillers use it as a signature aromatic alongside juniper.

q: Which is true of drinking customs in many Indian Adivasi communities?
o: Home-brewed drinks are offered to both guests and deities
r: Handia and similar brews carry ritual and hospitality roles alike.

q: Which best describes the Indian 'sundowner' culture inherited from colonial clubs?
o: A drink at sunset, often on a verandah or lawn
r: Gymkhana and planters' club culture left the sunset drink firmly in place.

q: Which is true about the availability of urrak outside Goa?
o: It is sold only in Mumbai
It is highly seasonal and rarely leaves the state
r: Roughly March to May only, and almost never beyond Goa.

q: Which cocktail template would best suit tamarind syrup?
o: A sour or a mule, where its tang balances sweetness
r: Imli's sweet-sour depth works beautifully with dark rum in a sour or a mule.

q: What does 'Indri' refer to in Indian whisky?
o: A single malt distillery in Haryana
r: Indri, Haryana, whose single malt won major international recognition.

q: Which is a distinctive feature of Goan drinking culture?
o: Susegad: unhurried, contented drinking, often with port-style wine or feni
r: Susegad, feni, urrak and Portuguese-legacy fortified wines together define it.

q: Which drink is most associated with a Kerala toddy shop meal?
o: Fresh toddy with fiery fish and duck curries
r: Kallu shaapus are destination restaurants as much as drinking spots.

q: What is 'ranu' in the context of handia?
o: A festival where it is drunk
An herbal starter tablet used to ferment the rice
r: Ranu tablets are hereditary herbal starters, passed down like heirlooms.

q: Which best describes the trajectory of Indian single malts since 2004?
o: From novelty to regularly beating Scotch in blind tastings and awards
They are all made by one distillery
r: Amrut, Paul John, Rampur and Indri have all won serious international recognition.

q: Which is true of vermouth's role in an Indian bar context?
o: Vermouth is only used in cooking
Imported and now some Indian-made vermouths support classic cocktails
r: Indian craft vermouths have joined imports as the cocktail scene matured.

q: Which pairing is correct?
o: All three come from palm sap
Mahua — cashew; Feni — palm sap; Toddy — flowers
Mahua — flowers; Feni — cashew; Toddy — palm sap
Mahua — palm sap; Feni — flowers; Toddy — cashew
r: Three different raw materials: mahua blossoms, cashew fruit, and palm sap.

q: Which is the odd one out among Indian traditional brews?
r: Tharra is a distilled country liquor from sugarcane; the other three are fermented rice brews.

q: Which statement about Indian beer is accurate?
o: Strong beer at 8% ABV or more holds a large market share
All Indian beer is under 5% ABV
r: 'Strong' beer is a distinctly large category in India, unlike most western markets.

q: What is the role of 'excise duty' in Indian alcohol?
o: A major state revenue source that shapes prices and availability
A central tax uniform across states
r: Excise is often among a state's largest own-revenue streams, which is why policies vary so much.

q: Which is true about tonic water in India today?
o: Craft Indian tonic brands now cater to the gin boom
r: Indian craft tonic brands grew alongside the local gin wave.

q: Which is the most accurate statement about 'IMFL whisky' and malt content?
o: It contains no alcohol from cane
Most contains little or no malt whisky, being largely molasses-based spirit
It is always blended with Scotch
r: This is precisely why the EU classifies it differently from grain whisky.

q: What is the significance of Mohan Meakin in Indian drinks history?
o: It founded India's first gin distillery
It is India's largest wine producer
It runs one of Asia's oldest breweries and distilleries and makes Old Monk
r: Its Kasauli and Solan operations date to the 19th century, and it makes Old Monk and Solan No.1.

q: Which is true about serving temperature for Indian summer coolers?
o: They are served very cold over ice to counter extreme heat
They are served at room temperature only
r: Shikanji, aam panna, chaas and jal-jeera are all built for heat relief.

q: Which best describes the future direction of Indian bartending, per current trends?
o: Regional ingredients, local spirits and low-waste methods gaining global recognition
r: Indian bars increasingly win recognition for regional identity rather than imitating western menus.

q: What is the most accurate statement about coconut feni versus cashew feni?
o: Coconut feni is distilled from coconut flesh
Coconut feni is made from palm sap, cashew feni from the cashew fruit
Cashew feni uses the nut, not the fruit
r: The cashew apple, not the nut, makes cashew feni. Coconut feni comes from palm sap.

q: Which is the correct order of strength, weakest to strongest, in typical serves?
r: Beer around 5%, wine 12–14%, fortified wine 15–20%, spirits 40%+.

q: Which Indian drink is simply spiced buttermilk?
r: Chaas is thinned, spiced buttermilk. Lassi is thicker and often sweet; thandai is a milk-and-nut drink.

q: Which of these is India's most famous beer brand?
r: Kingfisher. The others are all real Indian beers, but Kingfisher is the household name.

q: Rooh Afza is famous for which flavour?
r: A rose-forward sharbat concentrate, iconic across South Asia.

q: Which Indian state is most associated with feni and susegad drinking culture?
r: Goa, on both counts.

q: A 'burra peg' is what?
r: Burra means large, chota means small.

q: Which drink would you buy from a Mumbai gola cart?
r: Kala khatta, the sweet-sour-salty shaved-ice syrup.

q: Nimbu pani is another name for which drink?
r: Both names describe India's roadside spiced lemonade.

q: Which Indian city is India's wine capital?
r: Nashik, in Maharashtra, on the banks of the Godavari.

q: Which spirit does India consume the most of?
r: Whisky, by a very wide margin.

q: Thandai is traditionally drunk at which festival?
r: Holi, sometimes with bhang added.

q: Which is a Goan spirit made from cashew?
r: Cashew feni, made from the cashew apple rather than the nut.

q: Old Monk is which type of spirit?
r: A vatted Indian dark rum with a distinct vanilla character.

q: What is aam panna made to combat?
r: The tart raw-mango cooler that gets North India through the loo winds of May.

q: Which is a Himalayan millet brew served in a bamboo mug?
r: Tongba, drunk through a bamboo straw and topped up with hot water.

q: Toddy is tapped from which tree?
r: Palmyra, date and coconut palms all yield sap for toddy.

q: Which Indian drink uses roasted cumin as a defining flavour?
r: Jeera is cumin, and jal-jeera is built on it.

q: Which is a common Indian mixer for whisky?
r: Soda and water are the standard, alongside cola.

q: Kokum is grown mainly along which Indian coast?
r: The Konkan coast, where it becomes solkadhi and coolers.

q: Which is India's most common retail liquor bottle size, the 'quarter'?
r: 180 ml is the quarter; 90 ml is a nip.

q: Amrut is best known as India's first what?
r: India's first single malt, launched in Glasgow in 2004.

q: Which cocktail is gin and tonic's closest Indian historical relative?
o: The colonial quinine tonic taken against malaria
r: The G&T began as a way of making bitter antimalarial quinine drinkable.

q: Which of these Indian drinks contains no dairy?
r: Shikanji is lemon, sugar, salt and water. The other three are all milk or yogurt based.

q: Which Indian state is famous for its toddy shops serving fiery curries?
r: Kerala's kallu shaapus are destination restaurants.

q: What is jaggery, used in Indian drinks?
r: Unrefined cane sugar (gur), with caramel and mineral depth.

q: Which is a distilled spirit rather than a fermented brew?
r: Feni is distilled. Tongba, handia and Judima are all fermented.

q: Which Indian city is nicknamed the country's pub capital?
r: Bengaluru, since the draught-beer boom of the 1980s.

q: Which is true of alcohol regulation in India?
o: Only the central government issues licences
Rules are uniform across all states
Each state sets its own rules, so laws differ across borders
r: Alcohol is a state subject, which is why prices, ages and dry days all vary.

q: Which garnish would suit a kokum cooler?
r: Mint lifts the sour magenta fruit; the others fight it.

q: Which is a traditional Assamese rice wine with a GI tag?
r: Judima, of the Dimasa people, GI-tagged in 2021.

q: What does 'desi' mean in 'desi daru'?
r: Desi means local, so desi daru is country liquor.

q: Which is a real Indian craft gin brand?
r: Greater Than was among the first of India's craft gin wave.

q: Which best describes a 'dry day' in India?
o: A day when bars close early
A day with no ice available
A day when only beer is sold
A day when alcohol sales are prohibited
r: National holidays and polling days are commonly dry.

q: Which fruit gives jamun-based drinks their colour?
r: Jamun, the Indian blackberry, deep purple and astringent.

q: Which of these is served hot?
r: A whisky-spiked masala chai is India's winter answer to the hot toddy.

q: Solan No.1 is which kind of Indian spirit?
r: A whisky from Mohan Meakin, made in Himachal Pradesh.

q: Which is India's traditional drink offered during Holi in Varanasi's licensed shops?
r: Bhang stirred into thandai, sold at government-licensed shops.

q: What would you expect in a 'Monk and Coke'?
r: India's default order for generations.

q: Which is true of lassi?
o: A yogurt-based drink that can be sweet or salty
r: Yogurt blended with water, sweet (often mango) or salty (namkeen).

q: Which Indian spirit category has grown fastest with young urban drinkers?
r: The Goa-led craft gin wave.

q: Which is the correct base for a Nariyal Mojito?
r: The beach-shack mojito of coastal India, softened with tender coconut water.

q: Which is a Ladakhi drink ingredient?
r: Sea buckthorn, the tart 'leh berry' of the high Himalayas.

q: Which Indian drink is described as 'pink' and served after fish curry?
r: Kokum in coconut milk gives solkadhi its pale pink colour.

q: Which is the best-known Indian whisky brand by sales volume?
r: McDowell's No.1 is a mass-market giant; the others are premium single malts.

q: What is the traditional Indian vessel for lassi at a dhaba?
o: A tall steel or brass tumbler
r: Steel and brass tumblers are the everyday standard.

q: Which drink would a Goan bar most likely serve with lemonade and a slit chilli?
r: Urrak, the seasonal first distillation of feni, is drunk long with lemonade and chilli.

q: Which is a genuine Indian souring agent used in cocktails?
r: Kokum is Indian; yuzu is Japanese, calamansi Filipino, verjus European.

q: Which is true of Indian bar menus in the last decade?
o: Regional Indian ingredients have moved from novelty to standard
They have removed all local ingredients
r: Kokum, jamun, gondhoraj and curry leaf are now expected on serious Indian menus.

q: Which is a Punjabi and North Indian country liquor from sugarcane?
r: Tharra, distilled from fermented sugarcane or jaggery.

q: Which is true of black salt in Indian drinks?
o: It adds a savoury, sulphurous tang
r: Kala namak's distinctive savour defines many Indian coolers.

q: Which best describes khus?
r: Vetiver root, prized as a summer cooling flavour.

q: Which is the correct Indian name-to-drink match?
o: Chhaang — Himalayan barley or millet brew
r: Chhaang is the Himalayan fermented barley or millet brew.

q: Which Indian drink is made from fermented black carrots?
r: Kanji, fermented in the winter sun with mustard seeds, drunk around Holi.
